q: Consider the following as at the present date: 1-The 2023 reservation amendment is operative. 2-The new criminal statutes are in force. 3-The economic reservation has been upheld. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The reservation amendment awaits a census and delimitation.
why: Two current items are placed beside one that is enacted but inoperative, which is the distinction tested.
trapnote: In force, upheld and awaiting commencement are three different states. Place each item correctly.

q: Which statement about the criminal statutes in force from July 2024 is correct?
options: The requirement of production before a magistrate was dispensed with
Forensic examination became optional for offences punishable with seven years
The statutes replaced the Constitution's provisions on arrest and detention
Registration may be made irrespective of territorial jurisdiction
expl: Jurisdiction-free registration is among the changes; the other three are false.
why: The fourth option is structurally impossible and tests whether a candidate notices the category error.
trapnote: A statute cannot replace constitutional provisions. Watch for that category error.

q: Consider Andhra Pradesh: 1-It has twenty-six districts. 2-Its High Court sits at Amaravati. 3-Its Legislative Council was abolished in 2020. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: An abolition resolution was passed in 2020 but Parliament did not act, so the Council continues.
why: The resolution and the continuing Council coexist because the operative step was never taken.
trapnote: A resolution to abolish is not abolition. Parliament's law is the operative act.

q: Which of the following correctly states a change made in 2020?
options: The maximum strength of the lower House became 552
The maximum strength of the lower House became 550
The period of preventive detention without a Board became two months
Deemed assent was introduced for Bills pending with a Governor
expl: The ceiling fell when nominated seats were discontinued.
why: Each wrong option names a real proposition attached to the wrong year or never brought into force.
trapnote: One real change in 2020. The others belong to other years or never commenced.

q: Consider the November 2025 advisory opinion: 1-It concerned a Governor's assent to Bills. 2-It held that courts may not prescribe timelines. 3-It held deemed assent to be permissible. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: It held deemed assent to be impermissible.
why: The third statement states the April 2025 position, which the opinion set aside.
trapnote: Verify this item before the examination. It is the most recently changed rule in the syllabus.

q: Which statement about the 2024 nine-judge decision is correct?
options: It widened a Directive Principle and abolished the shield
It narrowed a Directive Principle and abolished the shield
It widened a Directive Principle and preserved the shield
It narrowed a Directive Principle and preserved the unamended shield
expl: Narrowed the directive; preserved the shield.
why: The four options exhaust every combination of two variables, so nothing can be eliminated by pattern.
trapnote: Two variables, four combinations. Settle each separately before reading off the pair.

q: Consider: 1-The economic reservation was upheld in 2022. 2-The ceiling was held not to be a basic feature. 3-Backward-class reservation may now exceed one-half freely. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The ceiling continues to bind the backward-class compartment.
why: The third statement generalises the holding beyond the compartment it concerned.
trapnote: The holding released one compartment from the ceiling. It did not release the other.

q: Which combination correctly describes what remains pending before the courts?
options: The economic reservation challenge and the validity of the 2020 amendment
The hill shrine reference and the scope of finality of a Money Bill certificate
The hill shrine reference and the validity of the criminal statutes of 2023
The Money Bill reference and the validity of the 2023 reservation amendment
expl: Both of those references remain undecided.
why: Each wrong option pairs one genuinely pending matter with one that has been decided or never challenged.
trapnote: Two live references. Keep them separate from matters already decided.

q: A candidate is told that district reorganisation in a State alters constitutional arrangements. Which statement is correct?
options: It alters administrative units alone and leaves constitutional provisions untouched
It alters the strength of the Legislative Assembly in proportion to the change
It alters the territorial jurisdiction of the High Court automatically
It alters the application of special constitutional provisions to the State
expl: Reorganisation of districts is an administrative exercise under State law.
why: Each wrong option attributes a constitutional consequence to an administrative act.
trapnote: Administrative change, constitutional continuity. The two do not move together.

q: Consider the six categories of distractor used throughout this course: 1-Number swap. 2-Institution swap. 3-Stage transplant. Which of these describes attaching a genuine requirement to the wrong step of a process?
options: 3 only
1 only
2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Only stage-transplant describes a genuine requirement at the wrong step.
why: Naming the category of a distractor is the fastest way to identify the planted option under time pressure.
trapnote: Name the trap to defeat it. Six categories cover almost every distractor in this paper.
